findings: The candidate depicts an identifiable adult male Purple Martin: iridescent dark blue-purple body, brown-black wings and tail, broad chest, small head, dark eye, stout slightly hooked bill, and long tapered wings agree with the references and live identification sources.
The main bird has one head, one beak, two wings—the far wing is naturally concealed by the side-on pose—two legs, two feet, and one forked tail. No duplicated or extraneous body parts are present.
The feet and tightly curled claws are somewhat simplified and oversized, but remain anatomically coherent for a perched swallow.
The detached wing study appears slightly broader and less sharply pointed than a Purple Martin's characteristically long, tapered wing. The main illustration conveys the wing shape more accurately.
The illustrated tail fork is slightly deeper and more elongated-looking than the typically short, moderately notched or forked Purple Martin tail, but not enough to create a material species error.

The common name, scientific name, family, length, weight, and wingspan are accurate. The habitat, cavity-nesting, migration, aerial-foraging, flocking, sexual-plumage, bill, wing, and tail statements are supported by the inspected sources.
